description: A hearty Kenyan chickpea stew slow-cooked with tomatoes, onions and spices. Popular as a filling vegetarian meal served with rice or chapati.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Add chopped onions and fry until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and curry powder. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce, about 8 minutes.
Add cooked chickpeas and 1 cup water. Stir well, season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with chapati or steamed rice.

name_sw: Mchuzi wa Maharagwe ya Kijani na Nazi
description: Fresh green beans simmered in a creamy coconut milk curry with tomatoes and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan side dish.

steps.instruction: Trim and cut the green beans into bite-sized pieces. Heat oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add garlic, curry powder and chopped tomatoes. Cook until the tomatoes soften into a sauce.
Add the green beans and coconut milk. Stir, season with salt and simmer for 10–12 minutes until the beans are tender but still bright.
Serve hot as a side with rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or grilled fish.

description: A refreshing Kenyan salad of cucumber, tomatoes and red onion tossed with lime juice and fresh coriander—the perfect side for grilled meats.

steps.instruction: Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons. Dice the tomatoes and finely chop the red onion.
Combine cucumber, tomato, onion and coriander in a bowl.
Squeeze lime juice over, sprinkle with salt and toss gently. Serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve alongside nyama choma, pilau or grilled fish.

description: A punchy Kenyan salsa built on sweet red onions, tomatoes, chilli and lime—the essential condiment at every Kenyan barbecue.

steps.instruction: Finely dice the red onion and tomatoes. Chop the coriander and chilli.
Mix everything in a bowl with lime juice and salt.
Let sit for 5 minutes to soften the onion, then serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or pilau.

description: A fluffy Kenyan omelette folded with chopped spring onions and a pinch of black pepper—a quick breakfast or light meal.

steps.instruction: Finely chop the spring onions. Whisk the eggs with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a frying pan. Add the spring onions and cook for 1 minute until softened.
Pour in the eggs and cook on low heat until set, then fold and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with chapati or toast.

description: A rustic Kenyan ugali made from sorghum flour, giving a nutty, earthy flavour and a slightly darker colour than maize ugali.

steps.instruction: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add the sorghum flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring and folding for 8–10 minutes until the ugali pulls away from the sides and forms a firm ball.
Shape into a mound and serve hot with a stew or greens.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki or beef stew.

description: A smooth, fermented millet porridge enjoyed warm for breakfast across Kenya, often sweetened with a little sugar.

steps.instruction: Mix the millet flour with 1 cup of water to make a smooth paste.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil. Stir in the millet paste and salt.
Cook on low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge thickens. Sweeten with sugar if desired and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve hot for breakfast, optionally with milk.

description: A stiff maize meal porridge, the undisputed staple of Kenya, served with vegetables, meat or fish.

steps.instruction: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add the ugali meal while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring and folding for 8–10 minutes until the ugali is firm and pulls away from the pot.
Turn out and shape into a mound. Serve hot with sukuma wiki, beans or meat.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki and beef stew.

description: A creamy Kenyan porridge of millet flour cooked in fresh milk, lightly sweetened — a nourishing breakfast for all ages.

steps.instruction: Mix millet flour with water to form a smooth paste.
Bring the fresh milk to a gentle boil. Stir in the millet paste and salt.
Cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Sweeten with sugar if desired and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve warm for breakfast.

description: Kenya's street food favourite — hard-boiled eggs split open and stuffed with a spicy tomato, onion, chilli and coriander salsa.

steps.instruction: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and slice each egg lengthwise about three-quarters of the way through.
Finely dice the tomato and red onion. Chop the coriander and chilli.
Mix the salsa with lime juice and salt. Spoon generously into the split eggs and serve immediately.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a street-style snack or breakfast.

name_sw: Sukuma Wiki ya Mafuta ya Nazi
description: Kale stir-fried in fragrant coconut oil with onions and tomatoes, adding a subtle tropical sweetness to Kenya's everyday greens.

steps.instruction: Wash and finely slice the kale. Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté onions until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften.
Add the kale and salt. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until tender but still bright green. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and grilled fish.

description: A simple Kenyan green vegetable stew wilted in groundnut oil with onions and tomatoes, finished with a scattering of crushed peanuts.

steps.instruction: Heat groundnut oil in a pan and sauté onions until golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and saucy.
Add the spinach and salt. Stir until wilted, about 5 minutes. Scatter with crushed groundnuts and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

description: Shredded cabbage stir-fried with onions, tomatoes and a generous pinch of curry powder—a quick, flavourful Kenyan side.

steps.instruction: Shred the cabbage finely. Heat oil and sauté onions until golden.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the cabbage and salt. Stir-fry for 8–10 minutes until tender. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with chapati or rice.

name_sw: Mchuzi wa Nyama ya Mchuzi Mix
description: A rich Kenyan beef stew seasoned with mchuzi mix, a beloved all-in-one spice blend that gives the gravy its signature savoury depth.

steps.instruction: Boil the beef with salt and water until tender, about 30–35 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Stir in the mchuzi mix, then add the beef and reserved broth. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until the stew thickens.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Crispy potato chips tossed in a spicy garam masala tomato gravy—a beloved Kenyan street food and late-night snack.

steps.instruction: Cut potatoes into chips and fry in hot oil until golden and crisp. Drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Stir in the garam masala and salt, then add the fried chips and toss until well coated. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a street snack or with kachumbari.

description: A fiery Kenyan salsa with fresh chilli, tomatoes, red onion and lime—for those who like their kachumbari with a serious kick.

steps.instruction: Finely chop the chilli, tomatoes, red onion and coriander.
Combine everything in a bowl with lime juice and salt.
Toss and serve fresh with grilled meat or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or pilau.

description: A fresh, herbaceous Kenyan chicken dish finished with a handful of chopped mint, giving a cooling contrast to the rich tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Brown the chicken pieces in hot oil for 6–8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Return the chicken to the pot, season with salt and simmer for 15–20 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the chopped mint just before serving.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: A soothing Kenyan tea made by steeping fresh lemongrass stalks with tea leaves and milk, popular for its calming citrus aroma.

steps.instruction: Bruise the lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife and place in a pot with water. Bring to a boil.
Add tea leaves and simmer for 3 minutes, then pour in the milk and sugar.
Simmer for another 3–4 minutes, strain and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a calming morning or evening tea.

description: Soft, fluffy Kenyan mandazi tossed in granulated sugar while still warm—a sweet teatime treat loved by children and adults alike.

steps.instruction: Mix the flour and salt. Add the milk and knead into a soft dough. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Roll out and cut into triangles. Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
While still warm, toss the mandazi in sugar until coated. Serve immediately.

serving_suggestion: Serve with tea or coffee.

name_sw: Mchuzi wa Nyama na Pilipili Hoho
description: Tender beef simmered with diced green pepper in a rich tomato gravy—the green pepper adds a fresh, grassy sweetness to the stew.

steps.instruction: Boil the beef until tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add the beef, diced green pepper and a little broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the pepper is tender and the sauce coats the meat.
Season with salt and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or ugali.

description: Tender tilapia fillets simmered in a spiced coconut sauce—a coastal Kenyan classic often served with rice.

steps.instruction: Season the tilapia fillets with salt. Heat oil and lightly fry the fillets for 2 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and curry powder and cook until saucy.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Return the fish to the pan and cook for 10–12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or chapati.

description: Dried dagaa (silver cyprinid) simmered in a tangy tomato-onion sauce with a squeeze of lemon—a nutritious lakeside staple.

steps.instruction: Rinse the dagaa and drain. Heat oil and fry the dagaa for 3–4 minutes until slightly crisp. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté onions until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Return the dagaa to the pan, add water and salt. Simmer for 8–10 minutes. Squeeze lemon juice over and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali.

description: Firm Nile perch steaks simmered in a rich tomato and onion gravy—a hearty fish stew from Lake Victoria.

steps.instruction: Season the Nile perch with salt. Heat oil and fry the fish for 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and green pepper and cook until saucy.
Add water and bring to a simmer. Return the fish to the pan and cook for 10 minutes until heated through and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Smoked fish gently simmered in a creamy coconut and tomato sauce—a rich, smoky stew from Kenya's lakeside communities.

steps.instruction: Soak the smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and flake into pieces.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Add the fish and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the stew thickens. Season with salt and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

description: A warm, probiotic Kalenjin porridge of millet flour stirred with sour milk (mursik), eaten for breakfast or as a nourishing drink.

steps.instruction: Mix the millet flour with 1 cup of water to form a smooth paste.
Bring the remaining water to a boil. Stir in the millet paste and cook for 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in the sour milk (and salt if using). Serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve warm for breakfast.
